title: The graph cone over a field and normalization branches
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $C	o\operatorname{Spec}k$ be locally of finite type, with every nonempty geometric fibre equidimensional of dimension one and every nonsmooth geometric point having completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. Put $D=\operatorname{Sing}(C/k)$ and let $\mathcal G=\mathcal G(C	o\operatorname{Spec}k,D\hookrightarrow C)$ be the graph conormal algebra [lem-sfb-graph-cone-gluing]. For $x\in D$ put $\kappa=\kappa(x)$, $A=\mathcal O_{C,x}$ and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_x$. Then $D$ is a possibly infinite disjoint union of open points $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$, with $\kappa(x)/k$ finite separable, and there is a canonical isomorphism of graded $\kappa$-algebras
$$\mathcal G\otimes_{\mathcal O_D}\kappa(x)\cong\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}A.$$
More precisely the local ring $H$ at the graph point in $C	imes_k\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$ is a localization of $A\otimes_k\kappa$; the graph ideal $J\subset H$ has quotient $H/J=\kappa$, its inverse image in $A$ is $\mathfrak m$, and the natural map $A	o H$ induces $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}A\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{gr}_JH$. Projectivizing gives
$$\operatorname{Proj}_{\kappa}(\mathcal G\otimes\kappa(x))\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A^
u/\mathfrak m A^
u)=C^
u	imes_C\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x),$$
where $C^
u$ is the reduced normalization and $A^
u$ the integral closure of $A_{m red}$ in its total ring of fractions. These intrinsic pointwise identifications assemble, even with infinitely many singular points, into a canonical isomorphism of $D$-schemes
$$\operatorname{Proj}_D\mathcal G\cong C^
u	imes_CD.$$
Over an algebraically closed geometric point the algebra $A^
u/\mathfrak m A^
u$ becomes $\Omega	imes\Omega$, whose two points correspond to the two geometric normalization branches. The isomorphisms are natural under isomorphisms of curves. Field, local finite type, geometric fibres, dimension, smoothness, completion, power series, residue field, separability, singular subscheme, associated graded, Proj, fibre products and reduced normalization are [def-weil-field], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-weil-pure-dimension], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], [def-weil-residue-field], [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme], [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring], [def-nagata-relative-proj], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization].

proof.text: Every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}S$ of $C$ has $S$ finite type over $k$. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), so $S$ is finitely presented over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]. This proves that $C/k$ is locally finitely presented. It is flat by [lem-pc-flat-field], and $C$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft]. These assertions are local and impose no quasi-compactness on $C$.

source.place: Tag 00FP (lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation); elementary field case and affine localization

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular] to $C/k$, using Step 1 and exactly the stipulated geometric-fibre hypotheses. It identifies the support of $D$ with the nonsmooth locus and says $D/k$ is unramified. Now [lem-trf-unramified-field-fibre-decomposition] gives $D=\coprod_{x\in D}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$, with each $\kappa(x)/k$ finite separable and each summand open. In particular $\mathcal O_{D,x}=\kappa(x)$. Each such $x$ is also closed in $C$: in any affine neighbourhood containing a specialization of $x$, the domain $S/\mathfrak p_x$ embeds in the finite-dimensional $k$-space $\kappa(x)$; it is therefore a finite-dimensional domain over $k$, hence a field, so $\mathfrak p_x$ is maximal.

The hypotheses needed for the local tangent-normalization theorem include pure dimension of $C$, rather than just its geometric fibre. Apply [lem-trf-geometric-pure-fibre-point-dimension] to the locally finitely presented map $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: the ordinary fibre is $C$, so its local topological dimension is $1$ at every point. Since $C$ is locally Noetherian, [lem-sbc-constant-local-dimension-components], with the open equal to $C$, shows that every irreducible component has dimension $1$. Thus $C$ is equidimensional of dimension one. At every $x\in D$, Step 2 supplies closedness and separability, and the original hypothesis supplies the geometric completed node.

source.place: Tag 00P4 (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-preserved-field-extension); varieties.tex Tag 0A21 (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic); topology.tex Tags 0055 and 0052

proof.text: Fix $x\in D$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}S\subset C$ containing it, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$ and $\kappa=S/\mathfrak p$. The graph over the open summand $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa\subset D$ lies in $U\times_k\operatorname{Spec}\kappa=\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_k\kappa)$. Its ring map is $e(s\otimes\lambda)=\bar s\lambda$; put $\mathfrak q=\ker e$. The affine fibre-product and stalk-localization statements give $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$ and $H=(S\otimes_k\kappa)_{\mathfrak q}$. Equivalently $H$ is the localization of $A\otimes_k\kappa$ at the kernel of the induced multiplication-to-$\kappa$ map: every $s\notin\mathfrak p$ has nonzero image in $\kappa$ and is inverted in both localizations, which proves the equivalence by their universal properties. The graph ideal is $J=\mathfrak qH$ and $H/J=\kappa$. The composite $A\to H\to\kappa$ is its residue map, so $J\cap A=\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Tag 0C4Y (lemma-change-fields-flat), localization description; schemes.tex Tags 01I4, 01JQ and 01JR

proof.text: In [lem-trf-separable-point-flat-completion-map], take its $K=F=\kappa$ and $\iota=\mathrm{id}_\kappa$, with the finite type algebra $S$ of Step 4. Its local ring $B$ is exactly $H$. Hence $A\to H$ is flat and $\mathfrak mH=J$, with induced residue map the identity on $\kappa$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-iso-mod-ideal-powers] to $I=\mathfrak m$: for all $n\ge1$ the canonical map $A/\mathfrak m^n\to H/\mathfrak m^nH=H/J^n$ is an isomorphism. (The equality of ideals follows by multiplying $\mathfrak mH=J$.) Then [lem-sfb-power-quotient-graded-comparison] gives the graded $\kappa$-algebra isomorphism $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}A\to\operatorname{gr}_JH$, with every homogeneous class $[a]$ sent to $[a\otimes1]$. This is the actual map induced by $A\to H$, not a choice of nodal coordinates.

source.place: Tag 0C54 (lemma-base-change-complete-local-ring), local map; algebra.tex Tag 051H (lemma-lift-basis), flat quotient-power consequence; associated-graded passage

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-graph-cone-gluing] to restrict $\mathcal G$ to the open component $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa\subset D$. In the affine graph neighbourhood of Step 4 its stalk is the conormal algebra at the graph point. By the explicit stalk formula in [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra], this is $\operatorname{gr}_JH$. Since $\mathcal O_{D,x}=\kappa$ and this component is an open one-point scheme, restriction, stalk and tensor with $\kappa(x)$ give the same graded algebra. Thus $\mathcal G\otimes_{\mathcal O_D}\kappa(x)\cong\operatorname{gr}_JH$. Compose with the inverse of Step 5 to obtain the required canonical isomorphism with $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}A$. The degree-zero identification is the identity on $\kappa$.

source.place: Tags 0631, 0632, 0633 (conormal algebra and lemma-affine-conormal-sheaf), applied at the graph stalk

proof.text:
The hypotheses for [lem-sfb-nodal-local-tangent-normalization] were verified in Steps 2--3. It gives intrinsically $\operatorname{Proj}_\kappa\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}A\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A^
u/\mathfrak m A^
u)$ and identifies the latter with $C^
u	imes_C\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$. Apply the homogeneous-localization construction of [def-sfb-relative-proj-iso-of-graded-iso] to Step 6, using its inverse where contravariance requires it. This gives exactly the asserted Proj isomorphism, with the structural map to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$ fixed. The same local theorem says $A^
u/\mathfrak m A^
u$ is separable quadratic and that its two geometric points are the normalized completed branches. In its split case it is $\kappa	imes\kappa$; in its field case it is a separable degree-two extension. Tensoring either algebra with an algebraically closed extension of $\kappa$ yields $\Omega	imes\Omega$ (in the field case its separable quadratic polynomial has two distinct roots).

For each open summand $D_x=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ of $D$, the affine restriction of [def-nagata-relative-proj] identifies $(\operatorname{Proj}_D\mathcal G)|_{D_x}$ with $\operatorname{Proj}_{\kappa(x)}(\mathcal G|_{D_x})$. Step 7 identifies this with $(C^\nu\times_CD)|_{D_x}$. These summands cover $D$ and distinct ones have empty intersection. Therefore the componentwise morphisms and their inverses glue uniquely to inverse morphisms over $D$. This argument uses arbitrary coproducts of open subschemes, not a finite cover; it applies unchanged to infinite $D$ and to $D=\varnothing$.

source.place: Open-cover gluing of scheme morphisms; relative Proj affine-restriction convention

proof.text: An isomorphism of curves carries $x$ to the corresponding singular point and carries the residue augmentation $e$ of Step 4 to its counterpart. The graph algebra restriction maps are natural by [lem-sfb-graph-cone-gluing]. The maps on quotient powers and graded rings commute with this square by [lem-sfb-power-quotient-graded-comparison], since on every class they send $[a]$ to the class of its image. The tangent-normalization identification is natural under the resulting pointed local-ring isomorphism by [lem-sfb-nodal-local-tangent-normalization]. Thus each local Proj comparison commutes with curve isomorphisms, and the unique gluing in Step 8 does too. No ordering of the two branches is chosen.
